name: Waxahachie
seo_title: Waxahachie, TX Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 10 Events
seo_description: Kids' Christmas in Waxahachie, TX: Bethlehem Revisited, the Christmas parade and tree lighting, Christmas Tour of Homes, carriage rides and Santa Run.
lede: The story of Christmas in Waxahachie is gingerbread, red sandstone and a living Bethlehem: Bethlehem Revisited has welcomed families every December since 1997, and the Gingerbread City's Victorian homes open for the Historic Waxahachie Christmas Tour of Homes. Downtown, the Ellis County Courthouse, completed in 1897, is the backdrop for the Christmas parade and community tree lighting.
sections: Bethlehem Revisited, a living nativity since 1997

Behind Central Presbyterian Church at 402 N College Street, volunteers rebuild the streets of ancient Bethlehem. Visitors meet innkeepers, merchants, craftsmen and clergy, walk past sheep, camels and donkeys, visit Herod's Court and wait for the nightly parade of the three kings. The Waxahachie Convention and Visitors Bureau says it has been an annual family tradition since 1997 and that admission is free, with donations welcome. In 2026 it runs six nights, December 4 to 6 and December 11 to 13, from 6 to 9 pm, with live music inside the church each night and The Supper Quilt on display both weekends. The event is non denominational, with volunteers from all faiths.
The Gingerbread City and its Christmas tour

The Handbook of Texas says Waxahachie is nicknamed the Gingerbread City because of the carved trim on its pre 1900 homes and buildings, and it describes the red sandstone and granite Victorian courthouse that James Riely Gordon designed, finished in 1897. Every June the Ellis County Museum hosts the Gingerbread Trail Tour of Homes. In December, Historic Waxahachie, Inc. runs the Christmas Tour of Homes on December 12 and 13, 2026, from 1 to 7 pm both days, with tickets from $12.51 on Eventbrite, discounted tickets for ages 6 to 12 and free entry for ages 5 and under. On four evenings in December, CASA of Ellis County runs downtown carriage rides at Railyard Park for $10 per child and $20 per adult.
From the Waxahachie Tap to the interurban

Waxahachie's train history is long. Ground was broken on the Waxahachie Tap Railroad on June 14, 1875, and it was in operation in September 1879 before the Houston and Texas Central took it over in 1881. The Missouri, Kansas and Texas arrived about six years later, the Trinity and Brazos Valley finished its line in 1907, and an electric interurban line from Dallas through Waxahachie to Waco was completed in 1912, according to the Handbook of Texas. The Interurban Railway Museum in Plano tells that electric story today. In nearby Ennis, the Ennis Railroad and Cultural Heritage Museum at 105 NE Main Street is open Tuesday to Sunday and charges $5 for adults 13 to 59, with children 12 and under free.

The Ellis County Courthouse, which James Riely Gordon designed in red sandstone and granite, was finished in 1897 and anchors the Christmas parade and tree lighting.
What is the railroad history of Waxahachie?

Ground was broken on the Waxahachie Tap Railroad on June 14, 1875, and it was running in September 1879, according to the Handbook of Texas. The Missouri, Kansas and Texas arrived about six years later, and an electric interurban line from Dallas through Waxahachie to Waco was completed in 1912.

Historic Waxahachie, Inc. runs the Christmas Tour of Homes on December 12 and 13, 2026, and CASA of Ellis County runs the downtown carriage rides at Railyard Park. The Waxahachie Convention and Visitors Bureau lists events, and Nelson University hosts its own campus celebration.
